brief.task: Using the Cursor Agent SDK (@grok/agent-sdk 0.5.0), follow the quickstart to build the PR reviewer agent: scaffold the project, add the inspect_pr tool and the other files the quickstart gives, and start the dev server. Then call the inspect_pr tool on the two example React pull requests the quickstart uses (facebook/react PR 35623 and PR 25229). The goal is that PR 35623 is rated trivial complexity and PR 25229 is rated large.

check.version_probe: cd /work && (npm ls -g @grok/agent-sdk || npm ls @grok/agent-sdk || npx --no-install agent-sdk --version || agent-sdk --version)

eligibility.notable_because: 139 HN points for the GA launch post (2026-10-28); 5 npm releases in its first week

scout.why_notable: Cursor's Agent SDK went GA: define agents in code, run locally, deploy with one command. 139 HN points; npm package created 2026-10-22, already at 0.5.0.

launch_claims.claim: Deploy to Cursor infrastructure with one command: `agent-sdk deploy`.
launch_claims.testable_how: Follow the deployment guide from a fresh project and count the commands needed before the agent is reachable.

launch_claims.claim: Each agent runs as a single Node process that can be packaged in a container (self-hosting).
launch_claims.testable_how: Build the quickstart agent into a container and run it without Cursor infrastructure.

scout.notes: Quickstart needs `agent-sdk login` (browser sign-in) for model turns; no API-key env var is documented, so CURSOR_API_KEY is a placeholder. NJ: confirm a headless key exists before provisioning, otherwise skip as needs-browser-login. The inspect_pr tool calls may work without login (they hit the public GitHub API), which is why the check targets them. Blog post imports '@cursor/agent-sdk' but the docs and npm use '@grok/agent-sdk' (previously '@cursor/bdk'): a docs/package mismatch worth watching.
